## Natural history notes

A small satyr butterfly characterized by soft brown wings with fine wavy lines and several small eyespots on the underside, closely resembling the Carolina Satyr and often requiring careful identification. In Florida, it is found in grassy clearings, wooded edges, swamps, hammock forests, wetland margins, and dry sandhill scrub where grasses and shaded or semi-shaded cover occur. Adults fly low and weakly through grasses and understory vegetation, feeding on moisture, sap, or other non-floral resources more often than showy flowers, while the caterpillars feed on grasses and overwinter as larvae.
